text:
Kai: noticed a perf regression after the latest kernel selector change. decode-heavy short requests are crowding the prefill queue, prefill throughput down ~18% :frowning:
Olivia: ugh, timeline? did selector start preferring fp16 kernels with small batch fast-paths? that can prioritize low-latency decode lanes
Kai: rolled 1812000000 change last night, it added a heuristic: choose kernel by instantaneous occupied threads. seems to bias toward short seqs -> lots of tiny decode batches.
Ryan: can you paste perf counters / p99 numbers? we need to see batching distribution
Kai: quick snapshot from canary:
- prefill p50/p95/p99: 12ms / 46ms / 210ms (was 10 / 28 / 120)
- decode p50/p95/p99: 5ms / 15ms / 60ms
- avg batch size prefill: 2.1 tokens
- avg batch size decode: 7.8 tokens
- KV cache hit ratio on prefill requests: 4% (expected ~22%)
Olivia: KV hit drop means prefill requests are getting split weirdly, probably because prefill queue isn't getting enough headroom for larger batches
Maya: hypothesis: the kernel selector's cost model underestimates per-token cost for prefill due to longer KV ops -> it routes to kernels that look faster for short sequences but kill aggregate throughput
Kai: experimented with enforcing a per-queue token budget. when we cap decode token budget to 30% of total tokens in-flight, prefill batch sizes rose to 4.7 and prefill p99 dropped to 140ms in local tests
Ryan: nice. config you used?
Kai: added these flags to runtime config (pseudo):
```
batching:
  token_budgets:
    prefill: 0.7
    decode: 0.3
  queue_isolation: true
  min_prefill_batch_tokens: 16
```
Olivia: min_prefill_batch_tokens helped a lot in sim? curious about cost impact on decode latency tail
Kai: decode p99 increased from 60ms -> 78ms (small), but overall throughput improved and user-facing generation rates recovered
Maya: let's A/B on canary: group A (current kernel selector) vs group B (selector + token budgets + min batch tokens). track p99 generation latency, cost per token, KV hit rate, and error rate over 2h windows
Ryan: I'll prepare rollout plan. small caveat: for customers on dedicated pools we should make token_budgets configurable per-tenant because they tune latencies differently
Olivia: also need to add a kernel-selection override that prefers kernels optimized for long-context prefill (different memory layout). that should be a simple extra term in the score: score += long_context_bias * expected_seq_len
Kai: agreed. I'll add a metric to the profiler to emit expected_seq_len histogram per-model so we can autotune long_context_bias
dev-bot: deploy-announce: canary group B (runtime v3.9.1-alpha) started at 1812345600
Maya: logging checklist: ensure KV cache eviction/warmer logs are present so we can correlate warms with batch size. add a small probe to sample KV warm latency for prefill flows
Ryan: I'll gate the rollout on KV warm latency not regressing >20% and prefill p99 < 150ms in the first 30m
Kai: will push the change and the probe. thanks team :thumbsup:
Olivia: one more: add a small smoke test that sends synthetic long-prefill single-shot requests to ensure the selector doesn't accidentally map them to tiny-kernel paths
Kai: noted, will add to our CI perf smoke harness
